headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise from shared workspace/file pathways; Notion AI’s vendor-hosted defaults make the pair unsafe without isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read/write the filesystem and execute shell commands, while Notion AI can access workspace pages and team knowledge base content. If AutoGPT ingests Notion-exported or copied content as instructions, prompt injection is plausible in default workflows. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF AutoGPT consumes Notion page exports or copied page text as instructions
IF a shared workspace file is used as a handoff channel between the agents
mitigations: Use a strict human review step before AutoGPT acts on any Notion-derived text
Keep Notion exports in a read-only folder separate from AutoGPT inputs
Prefix all handoff text with an instruction-free delimiter and strip prompts
Disable automated ingestion of workspace notes into AutoGPT
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all Notion-to-AutoGPT transfers

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI is vendor-hosted and sends content to Notion vendor backends/downstream model providers; AutoGPT has filesystem and shell access, so shared workspace content can be exposed if copied into its context or files. The profiles show overlapping access to workspace files, but no direct PHI/secrets claim, so medium fits the default leakage pathway.
conditions: IF the same workspace document is opened by Notion AI and then copied into AutoGPT context
IF AutoGPT reads files containing sensitive workspace content and transmits them via its network egress
mitigations: Restrict AutoGPT to a separate workspace with sanitized copies only
Avoid placing secrets or regulated data in pages that Notion AI can summarize
Turn off automatic sharing of AutoGPT outputs back into Notion pages
Review Notion page permissions before invoking AI on sensitive pages
requires-engineering: implement data-class labels and policy-based routing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, while Notion AI can modify workspace pages/databases within the user’s Notion permissions. They do not share the same write surface directly, but both can mutate user-controlled resources, so conflicting edits and race conditions are plausible when one agent’s output is copied into the other’s workspace. Uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF AutoGPT writes artifacts that are later pasted into Notion pages
IF Notion AI edits a page while AutoGPT is generating or updating related files
mitigations: Assign one agent as read-only for each shared artifact
Use timestamped filenames or page versions for handoffs
Manually reconcile edits before publishing
Keep AutoGPT outputs outside the live Notion workspace until approved
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency across the shared workflow

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is explicitly a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, so it may present AutoGPT-produced text as authoritative if copied into pages. AutoGPT can generate shell-driven outputs that Notion AI may summarize or reuse without verification. The pair therefore supports a default cascade from generated content to downstream action or documentation, but not enough evidence for high.
conditions: IF AutoGPT output is pasted into a Notion page that Notion AI later summarizes
IF Notion AI-generated summaries are used as the basis for AutoGPT follow-up actions
mitigations: Require a human to verify any AutoGPT-derived facts before saving them in Notion
Mark AI-generated sections clearly in workspace pages
Do not let Notion AI draft action items from unreviewed AutoGPT output
Cross-check citations against original sources before acting
requires-engineering: add verification gates between generation and execution

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI is vendor-hosted and uses Notion workspace permissions plus downstream model providers, while AutoGPT is open-source and locally runnable with filesystem and shell access. If regulated workspace content is processed by Notion AI and then handled by AutoGPT, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the higher safe choice.
conditions: IF regulated or residency-bound content is stored in Notion pages processed by Notion AI
IF AutoGPT is used to export or reprocess the same content outside the approved retention policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Notion AI-enabled pages
Use separate workspaces for compliant and non-compliant content
Review vendor retention settings before enabling AI on sensitive pages
Document which data classes may flow through each agent
requires-engineering: obtain a DPA and residency review for the full workflow
